claim: Kupffer's vesicle (KV) is a transient organ with a fluid-filled lumen in zebrafish embryos.
source: Kupffer's vesicle (KV), a transient organ with a fluid-filled lumen, provides a simple system to investigate the interplay between intrinsic cellular mechanisms and external forces during epithelial morphogenesis.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a description of the KV organ system.

claim: Asymmetric cell volume changes occur along the anteroposterior axis of KV during development.
source: Using 3-dimensional (3D) analyses of single cells we identify asymmetric cell volume changes along the anteroposterior axis of KV that coincide with asymmetric cell shape changes.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 2G.

claim: Blocking ion flux prevents cell volume changes and cell shape changes in KV.
source: Blocking ion flux prevents these cell volume changes and cell shape changes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 3.

claim: Vertex simulations suggest cell shape changes do not depend on lumen expansion.
source: Vertex simulations suggest cell shape changes do not depend on lumen expansion.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by modeling results in Figure 4.

claim: Asymmetric changes in KV cell volume and shape occur normally when KV lumen growth fails due to leaky cell adhesions.
source: Consistent with this prediction, asymmetric changes in KV cell volume and shape occur normally when KV lumen growth fails due to leaky cell adhesions.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 6.

claim: Ion flux mediates cell volume changes that contribute to asymmetric cell shape changes in KV.
source: These results indicate ion flux mediates cell volume changes that contribute to asymmetric cell shape changes in KV, and that these changes in epithelial morphology are separable from lumen-generated forces.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental and modeling results.

claim: Changes in epithelial morphology in KV are separable from lumen-generated forces.
source: These results indicate ion flux mediates cell volume changes that contribute to asymmetric cell shape changes in KV, and that these changes in epithelial morphology are separable from lumen-generated forces.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental and modeling results.

claim: KV functions as a 'left-right organizer' to determine left-right asymmetry of the zebrafish embryo.
source: KV, which functions as a 'left-right organizer' to determine left-right asymmetry of the zebrafish embryo (Essner et al., 2005; Kramer-Zucker et al., 2005), is a transient organ comprised of a single layer of ~50 epithelial cells that surround a fluid-filled lumen.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: KV is comprised of a single layer of approximately 50 epithelial cells that surround a fluid-filled lumen.
source: KV, which functions as a 'left-right organizer' to determine left-right asymmetry of the zebrafish embryo (Essner et al., 2005; Kramer-Zucker et al., 2005), is a transient organ comprised of a single layer of ~50 epithelial cells that surround a fluid-filled lumen.
evidence: This is a descriptive statement about KV structure in the introduction.

claim: Each KV cell extends a motile monocilium into the lumen to generate asymmetric fluid flows.
source: Each KV cell extends a motile monocilium into the lumen to generate asymmetric fluid flows that direct left-right patterning signals.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a functional characteristic of KV cells.

claim: Dorsal forerunner cells (DFCs) differentiate into epithelial KV cells at the end of gastrulation stages.
source: Fate mapping studies have identified precursor cells, called dorsal forerunner cells (DFCs), which differentiate into epithelial KV cells at the end of gastrulation stages of development (Melby et al., 1996; Cooper and D'Amico, 1996).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: KV cells form a rosette-like structure to give rise to a nascent lumen that expands over time.
source: Similar to other organs that develop a fluid-filled lumen—such as the gut tube (Alvers et al., 2014) or pancreas (Villasenor et al., 2010)—KV cells form a rosette-like structure to give rise to a nascent lumen that expands over time (Amack et al., 2007; Oteíza et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: KV cells at the anterior half (KV-ant cells) develop columnar morphologies at later stages of development.
source: KV cells have similar shapes at early stages of development, whereas at later stages the cells in the anterior half of KV (KV-ant cells) develop columnar morphologies that allow tight packing of these cells and posterior KV cells (KV-post cells) become wide and thin (Wang et al., 2012) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Posterior KV cells (KV-post cells) become wide and thin at later stages of development.
source: KV cells have similar shapes at early stages of development, whereas at later stages the cells in the anterior half of KV (KV-ant cells) develop columnar morphologies that allow tight packing of these cells and posterior KV cells (KV-post cells) become wide and thin (Wang et al., 2012) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: KV remodeling results in an AP asymmetric distribution of cilia that is necessary to drive fluid flows for left-right patterning.
source: This morphogenetic process, which we refer to as 'KV remodeling', results in an AP asymmetric distribution of cilia that is necessary to drive fluid flows for left-right patterning (Wang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Actomyosin contractility and differential interfacial tensions between KV cells mediate asymmetric cell shape changes.
source: Experimental results and mathematical simulations from our group indicate that actomyosin contractility and differential interfacial tensions between KV cells mediate asymmetric cell shape changes (Wang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: AP asymmetric deposition of extracellular matrix (ECM) is implicated in restricting anterior KV cell shape during KV lumen expansion.
source: Additional studies identified an AP asymmetric deposition of extracellular matrix (ECM) implicated in restricting anterior KV cell shape during KV lumen expansion (Compagnon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: KV-ant cells increase their volume during KV morphogenesis.
source: 3D analyses revealed that KV-ant cells increase their volume and KV-post cells decrease their volume during KV morphogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a finding from 3D analyses and supported by data in Figure 2G.

claim: KV-post cells decrease their volume during KV morphogenesis.
source: 3D analyses revealed that KV-ant cells increase their volume and KV-post cells decrease their volume during KV morphogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a finding from 3D analyses and supported by data in Figure 2G.

claim: KV cell volume and shape changes are mediated by ion channel activity that regulates ion flux and fluid transport.
source: At the molecular level, KV cell volume and shape changes are mediated by ion channel activity that regulates ion flux and fluid transport.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by experimental data in Figure 3.

claim: When external tissues are solid-like, asymmetric cell volume changes in KV cells contribute to cell shape changes even in the absence of lumen expansion.
source: Models predicted that when external tissues are solid-like, asymmetric cell volume changes in KV cells contribute to cell shape changes even in the absence of lumen expansion.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a prediction from mathematical models and supported by modeling results in Figure 4.

claim: Changes in KV cell volume and shape can occur independent of forces associated with lumen growth.
source: Consistent with mathematical model predictions, experimental perturbations of lumen expansion indicated that changes in KV cell volume and shape can occur independent of forces associated with lumen growth.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by experimental data in Figure 6.

claim: The Tg(sox17:GFP-CAAX) transgenic strain provides bright labeling of KV cell membranes with green fluorescent protein (GFP).
source: A transgenic strain developed in this study, Tg(sox17:GFP-CAAX), provides bright labeling of KV cell membranes with green fluorescent protein (GFP) that shows the AP asymmetric architecture of the whole organ (Video 1) and the 2D shapes of epithelial KV cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with reference to Video 1 and Figure 1A.

claim: Brief treatment of double transgenic Tg(sox17:CreERT2); Tg(ubi:Zebrabow) embryos with 4-OHT from the dome stage to the shield stage generates low levels of Cre activity.
source: Brief treatment of double transgenic Tg(sox17:CreERT2); Tg(ubi:Zebrabow) embryos with 4-OHT from the dome stage to the shield stage generates low levels of Cre activity that changes expression of default RFP to expression of YFP in a subset of KV cells.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 1D and supported by the image in Figure 1E.

claim: Cell height of both KV-ant cells and KV-post cells increased from 2 ss to 8 ss.
source: First, cell height of both KV-ant cells and KV-post cells increased from 2 ss to 8 ss (Figure 2C), reflecting the expansion of the apical surface of cells (see dotted line in Figure 2B) to accommodate lumen growth.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: There were no significant differences in cell height between KV-ant cells and KV-post cells during stages from 2 ss to 8 ss.
source: There were no significant differences in cell height between KV-ant cells and KV-post cells during these stages (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: Cell length decreased in both KV-ant cells and KV-post cells during KV morphogenesis, but a sharp reduction was observed from 4 ss to 6 ss in KV-post cells.
source: Second, cell length decreased in both KV-ant cells and KV-post cells during KV morphogenesis, but a sharp reduction was observed from 4 ss to 6 ss in KV-post cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 2D.

claim: The cell length of KV-post cells became significantly different from KV-ant cells after 4 ss.
source: This resulted in the cell length of KV-post cells to become significantly different from KV-ant cells after 4 ss.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2D.

claim: KV-ant cells remained relatively constant in width during KV morphogenesis.
source: Third, analysis of cell width indicated KV-ant cells remained relatively constant during KV morphogenesis, whereas KV-post cells showed a distinctive increase in width between 4 ss and 6 ss that resulted in significant differences between KV-ant cells and KV-post cells after 4 ss (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 2E.

claim: KV-post cells showed a distinctive increase in width between 4 ss and 6 ss.
source: Third, analysis of cell width indicated KV-ant cells remained relatively constant during KV morphogenesis, whereas KV-post cells showed a distinctive increase in width between 4 ss and 6 ss that resulted in significant differences between KV-ant cells and KV-post cells after 4 ss (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 2E.

claim: Both KV-ant and KV-post cells had similar morphologies at 2 ss and 4 ss.
source: We found that both KV-ant and KV-post cells had similar morphologies at 2 ss and 4 ss and that these morphologies changed after 4 ss such that KV-ant cells had a significantly larger LWR than KV-post cells (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 2F.

claim: KV-ant cells had a significantly larger LWR than KV-post cells after 4 ss.
source: We found that both KV-ant and KV-post cells had similar morphologies at 2 ss and 4 ss and that these morphologies changed after 4 ss such that KV-ant cells had a significantly larger LWR than KV-post cells (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 2F.

claim: At 2 ss and 4 ss, KV-ant and KV-post cells showed similar cell volumes.
source: At 2 ss and 4 ss, KV-ant and KV-post cells showed similar cell volumes (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 2G.

claim: Between 4 ss to 6 ss, the volume of KV-ant cells increased and the volume of KV-post cells decreased.
source: However, between 4 ss to 6 ss—when KV cells change shape—the volume of KV-ant cells increased and the volume of KV-post cells decreased (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 2G.

claim: Cell volume becomes significantly different between KV-ant and KV-post cells after 4 ss.
source: Our results indicate cell volume becomes significantly different between KV-ant and KV-post cells after 4 ss (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 2G.

claim: Between 2 ss and 8 ss, KV-ant cells increased volume from 2106 ± 1014 μm3 to 2547 ± 693 μm3.
source: Overall, between 2 ss and 8 ss, KV-ant cells increased volume from 2106 ± 1014 μm3 to 2547 ± 693 μm3 (shown are mean ±one standard deviation) and KV-post cell decreased volume from 2180 ± 1034 μm3 to 1564 ± 539 μm3 (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 2G.

claim: Between 2 ss and 8 ss, KV-post cells decreased volume from 2180 ± 1034 μm3 to 1564 ± 539 μm3.
source: Overall, between 2 ss and 8 ss, KV-ant cells increased volume from 2106 ± 1014 μm3 to 2547 ± 693 μm3 (shown are mean ±one standard deviation) and KV-post cell decreased volume from 2180 ± 1034 μm3 to 1564 ± 539 μm3 (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 2G.

claim: KV-ant cells always increase in volume and KV-post cells always decrease in volume during development.
source: It is important to note that while the cell sizes are variable, the direction of size changes during development is constant. KV-ant cells always increase in volume and KV-post cells always decrease in volume.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an observation about the consistency of volume changes.

claim: Total KV-ant cellular volume and total KV-post cellular volume were similar at 2 ss, but then were significantly different at 8 ss.
source: Volume measurements indicated that both 'total KV-ant cellular volume' and 'total KV-post cellular volume' were similar at 2 ss, but then were significantly different at 8 ss (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Total KV-ant cellular volume increased from 1.4 × 105 μm3 to 1.7 × 105 μm3 between 2 ss and 8 ss stages.
source: Overall, 'total KV-ant cellular volume' increased from 1.4 × 105 μm3 to 1.7 × 105 μm3 and 'total KV-post cell volume' decreased from 1.2 × 105 μm3 to 0.98 × 105 μm3 between 2 ss and 8 ss stages (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Total KV-post cell volume decreased from 1.2 × 105 μm3 to 0.98 × 105 μm3 between 2 ss and 8 ss stages.
source: Overall, 'total KV-ant cellular volume' increased from 1.4 × 105 μm3 to 1.7 × 105 μm3 and 'total KV-post cell volume' decreased from 1.2 × 105 μm3 to 0.98 × 105 μm3 between 2 ss and 8 ss stages (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Cellular volume can be controlled through coordinated flux of Na+, K+ and Cl- ions via specific ion channels and pumps that results in osmotically driven water transport.
source: At the molecular level, cellular volume can be controlled through coordinated flux of Na+, K+ and Cl- ions via specific ion channels and pumps that results in osmotically driven water transport (Wilson et al., 2007; Barrett and Keely, 2000; Frizzell and Hanrahan, 2012; Frizzell, 1995; Damkier et al., 2013; Spring and Siebens, 1988; Hoijman et al., 2015; Saias et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with supporting citations.

claim: Both Na+/K+-ATPase and Cftr have previously been shown to play a role in KV lumen expansion.
source: To test whether cell volume changes in KV cells are mediated by ion flux, we inhibited either the sodium-potassium pump (Na+/K+-ATPase) or the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (Cftr). Both have previously been shown to play a role in KV lumen expansion (Navis et al., 2013; Compagnon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with supporting citations.

claim: Embryos treated with ouabain from the bud stage (10 hpf) to 8 ss (13 hpf) showed reduced KV lumen expansion.
source: In contrast, embryos treated with ouabain from the bud stage (10 hpf) to 8 ss (13 hpf) did show reduced KV lumen expansion (Figure 3B,E) relative to vehicle (DMSO; dimethyl sulfoxide) treated controls (Figure 3A,E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3B,E.

claim: In control embryos treated with DMSO from bud stage to 8 ss, KV-ant cells increased volume from 2019 ± 668 μm3 to 2304 ± 618 μm3.
source: Similar to wild-type embryos, mosaic labeled KV cells in control embryos treated with DMSO from bud stage to 8 ss underwent normal AP asymmetric changes in cell volume and shape (Figure 3A). KV-ant cells increased volume from 2019 ± 668 μm3 to 2304 ± 618 μm3 and KV-post cells decreased volume from 1811 ± 422 μm3 to 1479 ± 323 μm3 between 2 ss and 8 ss (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: In control embryos treated with DMSO from bud stage to 8 ss, KV-post cells decreased volume from 1811 ± 422 μm3 to 1479 ± 323 μm3.
source: Similar to wild-type embryos, mosaic labeled KV cells in control embryos treated with DMSO from bud stage to 8 ss underwent normal AP asymmetric changes in cell volume and shape (Figure 3A). KV-ant cells increased volume from 2019 ± 668 μm3 to 2304 ± 618 μm3 and KV-post cells decreased volume from 1811 ± 422 μm3 to 1479 ± 323 μm3 between 2 ss and 8 ss (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: AP asymmetric cell volume changes were not observed in embryos treated with ouabain between bud stage and 8 ss.
source: In contrast, AP asymmetric cell volume changes were not observed in embryos treated with ouabain between bud stage and 8 ss.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3B.

claim: In ouabain treated embryos, both KV-ant and KV-post cells increased volume from 1920 ± 548 μm3 to 2328 ± 1050 μm3 and from 1819 ± 514 μm3 to 2407 ± 493 μm3 respectively.
source: In ouabain treated embryos both KV-ant and KV-post cells increased volume from 1920 ± 548 μm3 to 2328 ± 1050 μm3 and from 1819 ± 514 μm3 to 2407 ± 493 μm3 respectively (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: Treating embryos with 30 μM CFTRinh-172 from bud stage to 8 ss reduced KV lumen expansion.
source: Treating embryos with 30 μM CFTRinh-172 from bud stage to 8 ss reduced KV lumen expansion (Figure 3C,E) as expected (Roxo-Rosa et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3C,E and a supporting citation.

claim: CFTRinh-172 treatments eliminated asymmetric volume changes in KV cells.
source: Similar to ouabain treatments, CFTRinh-172 treatments eliminated asymmetric volume changes in KV cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3C.

claim: In CFTRinh-172 treated embryos, KV-post cells did not lose volume, but rather increased in volume from 1878 ± 361 μm3 to 2123 ± 632 μm3.
source: In contrast to controls (Figure 3A), KV-post cells in CFTRinh-172 treated embryos did not lose volume, but rather increased in volume from 1878 ± 361 μm3 to 2123 ± 632 μm3.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3C.

claim: In CFTRinh-172 treated embryos, KV-ant cells increased in volume from 1513 ± 289 μm3 to 1944 ± 483 μm3.
source: KV-ant cells increased in volume from 1513 ± 289 μm3 to 1944 ± 483 μm3 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3C.

claim: Reducing Cftr expression by injecting embryos with cftr MO had effects that were similar to CFTRinh-172 treatments: KV lumen failed to expand and asymmetric cell volume changes were disrupted.
source: Reducing Cftr expression by injecting embryos with cftr MO had effects that were similar to CFTRinh-172 treatments: KV lumen failed to expand and asymmetric cell volume changes were disrupted (Figure 3D,E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3D,E.

claim: In cftr MO treated embryos, both KV-ant and KV-post cells increased their volume from 1872 ± 726 μm3 to 2252 ± 842 μm3 and from 2082 ± 637 μm3 to 2367 ± 770 μm3 respectively.
source: In cftr MO treated embryos both KV-ant and KV-post cells increased their volume from 1872 ± 726 μm3 to 2252 ± 842 μm3 and from 2082 ± 637 μm3 to 2367 ± 770 μm3 respectively (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3D.

claim: In both CFTRinh-172 and cftr MO treated embryos, KV-post cells fail to undergo volume loss due to inhibition of fluid efflux from these cells.
source: This suggests that in both CFTRinh-172 and cftr MO treated embryos KV-post cells fail to undergo volume loss due to inhibition of fluid efflux from these cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results section based on the experimental data.

claim: Ion flux regulated by Na+/K+-ATPase and Cftr activity is a mechanism that drives asymmetric changes in KV cell volumes along the AP axis.
source: Taken together (for statistical power analysis, see Figure 3—source data 1), these results indicate ion flux regulated by Na+/K+-ATPase and Cftr activity is a mechanism that drives asymmetric changes in KV cell volumes along the AP axis.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data.

claim: The height (apical surfaces) of KV cells did not increase between 2 ss and 8 ss in embryos treated with inhibitors of Na+/K+-ATPase or Cftr activity as they did in controls.
source: The height (apical surfaces) of KV cells did not increase between 2 ss and 8 ss in embryos treated with inhibitors of Na+/K+-ATPase or Cftr activity as they did in controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B), which is consistent with a failure of lumen expansion.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: AP asymmetric cell shape changes observed in control embryos between 2 ss and 8 ss failed to occur in embryos treated with ouabain or Cftr inhibitors.
source: Analysis of length to width ratios (LWRs) of individual KV-ant and KV-post cells revealed that AP asymmetric cell shape changes observed in control embryos between 2 ss and 8 ss (Figure 3A) failed to occur in embryos treated with ouabain or Cftr inhibitors (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3A-D.

claim: Ion flux is necessary for both cell volume changes and cell shape changes during KV remodeling.
source: These results indicated that ion flux is necessary for both cell volume changes and cell shape changes during KV remodeling.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data.

claim: The overall morphology of ouabain treated embryos was similar to controls at 8 ss, except the KV lumen was smaller.
source: The overall morphology of ouabain treated embryos was similar to controls at 8 ss, except the KV lumen was smaller (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A,B), indicating ouabain treatments did not cause severe developmental defects.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 3A,B.

claim: There was no significant difference in cell shapes at 2 ss or 8 ss stages between control or ouabain treated embryos for cells surrounding KV.
source: Analysis of external cells with clearly defined boundaries (mCherry-CAAX labeling) that were positioned either anterior or posterior of KV indicated that there was no significant difference in cell shapes at 2 ss or 8 ss stages between control or ouabain treated embryos (Figure 3—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 3D.

claim: Ouabain does not alter the shapes of cells surrounding KV.
source: These results indicate that ouabain does not alter the shapes of cells surrounding KV and suggest that defects in KV cell shape changes result from altered ion flux in KV.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data.

claim: Vertex models represent two-dimensional cross-sections of cells in a tissue as a network of edges and vertices.
source: Vertex models, which have been used successfully by our group and others for predicting features of developing tissues (Fletcher et al., 2014; Bi et al., 2015; Farhadifar et al., 2007; Hufnagel et al., 2007; Wang et al., 2012), represent two-dimensional cross-sections of cells in a tissue as a network of edges and vertices, as shown in Figure 4A–D.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with supporting citations and reference to Figure 4A-D.

claim: Changes in cell cross-sectional areas correlated with the corresponding cell volume changes.
source: We first measured the cross-sectional areas of KV cells within this plane and found that changes in cell cross-sectional areas correlated with the corresponding cell volume changes (Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 4—source data 1.

claim: The APA is never above 0.31 in the vertex model simulations, which is much smaller than wild-type experimental observations.
source: A first observation is that the APA is never above 0.31, which is much smaller than wild-type experimental observations.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an observation from the modeling results.

claim: Changes to cross-sectional area may be an important contribution to shape remodeling, but alone they are not sufficient to generate the observed shape changes.
source: This suggests that changes to cross-sectional area may be an important contribution to shape remodeling, but alone they are not sufficient to generate the observed shape changes.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the modeling results.

claim: The model predicts that cross-sectional area changes drive the observed shape changes primarily in the solid-solid region.
source: Interestingly, our model predicts that cross-sectional area changes drive the observed shape changes primarily in the solid-solid region, and our understanding of the fluid-solid transition helps us to understand this effect (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 4G.

claim: When the external cells are fluid-like, the KV cells are able to slide past the external cells, so that the interface between the KV-ant and KV-post cells moves towards the posterior as the area of the KV-post cells is reduced.
source: When the external cells are fluid-like, the KV cells are able to slide past the external cells, so that the interface between the KV-ant and KV-post cells (indicated by a thick black line in Figure 4G) moves towards the posterior as the area of the KV-post cells is reduced.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 4G.

claim: When the external cells are solid-like, the interface between the KV-ant and KV-post cells is pinned.
source: In contrast, when the external cells are solid-like, the interface between the KV-ant and KV-post cells is pinned.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a mechanism from the modeling results.

claim: When the KV-post cells lose area and the external cells are solid-like, they must maintain their lateral width and so the apico-basal extension must decrease.
source: In this second case, when the KV-post cells lose area they must maintain their lateral width and so the apico-basal extension must decrease.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a mechanism from the modeling results.

claim: The proposed mechanism works equally well in 3D as in 2D -- solid-like external tissue would pin the anterior-posterior interface so that cell volume changes would affect the area of lateral interfaces between KV cells but not the apical area in contact with the lumen.
source: We note that this proposed mechanism works equally well in 3D as in 2D -- solid-like external tissue would pin the anterior-posterior interface so that cell volume changes would affect the area of lateral interfaces between KV cells but not the apical area in contact with the lumen.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an interpretation of the modeling results.

claim: In 3D, asymmetric cell volume changes would lead to asymmetric cell shape changes and similar APA values to the ones identified in the 2D model.
source: Therefore, in 3D asymmetric cell volume changes would lead to asymmetric cell shape changes and similar APA values to the ones we identified in our 2D model.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a prediction from the modeling results.

claim: The simple model suggests that asymmetric cell volume changes contribute to cell shape changes, though additional mechanisms are necessary to explain the very high APA values that are observed in experiments.
source: Although we cannot rule out a more complex model for KV cell shape changes (e.g. with additional parameters characterizing the mechanical heterogeneities in each cell), our simple model suggests that asymmetric cell volume changes contribute to cell shape changes, though additional mechanisms are necessary to explain the very high APA values that are observed in experiments.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the modeling results.

claim: In an environment in which cells have solid-like mechanical properties, asymmetric volume changes in KV cells can partially drive asymmetric KV cell shape changes even in the absence of lumen expansion.
source: These results suggest that in an environment in which cells have solid-like mechanical properties, asymmetric volume changes in KV cells can partially drive asymmetric KV cell shape changes even in the absence of lumen expansion (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section with reference to Figure 4H.

claim: AP cell asymmetry was much more pronounced if only the anterior external cells were solid-like than if only the posterior external cells were solid-like.
source: We found that AP cell asymmetry was much more pronounced if only the anterior external cells were solid-like (Figure 4—figure supplement 4A) than if only the posterior external cells were solid-like (Figure 4—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 4A,B.

claim: Solidity of only anterior external cells can be sufficient to introduce an asymmetry in KV cell shapes that can be slightly stronger than if all external cells were solid-like.
source: Thus, solidity of only anterior external cells can be sufficient to introduce an asymmetry in KV cell shapes that can be slightly stronger than if all external cells were solid-like.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the modeling results.

claim: Asymmetry in the mechanical properties of the cells (and/or material) surrounding the KV can support asymmetric cell shape changes in KV.
source: Hence, asymmetry in the mechanical properties of the cells (and/or material) surrounding the KV can support asymmetric cell shape changes in KV.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the modeling results.

claim: E-cadherin is expressed in KV cells.
source: E-cadherin is expressed in KV cells (Matsui et al., 2011; Tay et al., 2013), but loss of E-cadherin function in mutant embryos leads to early developmental defects during epiboly that preclude analysis of KV formation (Kane et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with supporting citations.

claim: Loss of E-cadherin function in mutant embryos leads to early developmental defects during epiboly that preclude analysis of KV formation.
source: E-cadherin is expressed in KV cells (Matsui et al., 2011; Tay et al., 2013), but loss of E-cadherin function in mutant embryos leads to early developmental defects during epiboly that preclude analysis of KV formation (Kane et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a supporting citation.

claim: Transcriptome analysis of zebrafish KV cells indicated that Junction plakoglobin (Jup; also called γ-catenin) is expressed in KV cells.
source: Transcriptome analysis of zebrafish KV cells (unpublished data) indicated that Junction plakoglobin (Jup; also called γ-catenin) is expressed in KV cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on unpublished data.

claim: Jup interacts in complexes at cell-cell adhesions.
source: Jup interacts in complexes at cell-cell adhesions (Fukunaga et al., 2005; Lewis et al., 1997) and is thought to link cadherins to the cytoskeleton (Kowalczyk et al., 1998; Leonard et al., 2008; Holen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with supporting citations.

claim: Jup is thought to link cadherins to the cytoskeleton.
source: Jup interacts in complexes at cell-cell adhesions (Fukunaga et al., 2005; Lewis et al., 1997) and is thought to link cadherins to the cytoskeleton (Kowalczyk et al., 1998; Leonard et al., 2008; Holen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with supporting citations.

claim: Jup plays an essential role in maintaining cell-cell adhesions.
source: Previous studies in cell cultures indicated Jup plays an essential role in maintaining cell-cell adhesions (Fang et al., 2014) and that perturbing Jup function results in increased epithelial permeability (Nottebaum et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with supporting citations.

claim: Perturbing Jup function results in increased epithelial permeability.
source: Previous studies in cell cultures indicated Jup plays an essential role in maintaining cell-cell adhesions (Fang et al., 2014) and that perturbing Jup function results in increased epithelial permeability (Nottebaum et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with supporting citations.

claim: RNA in situ hybridizations confirmed jupa expression in KV cells and the population of precursor cells that give rise to KV called dorsal forerunner cells (DFCs).
source: RNA in situ hybridizations confirmed jupa expression in KV cells and the population of precursor cells that give rise to KV called dorsal forerunner cells (DFCs) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Jupa protein is localized to lateral membranes of KV cells.
source: Immunofluorescence experiments using Jup antibody (Martin et al., 2009) indicated Jupa protein is localized to lateral membranes of KV cells that are marked by GFP expression in Tg(sox17:GFP-CAAX) embryos (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5A and a supporting citation.

claim: Interfering with Jupa function would perturb KV cell-cell junction integrity such that the KV lumen would fail to expand properly.
source: Thus, we predicted that interfering with Jupa function would perturb KV cell-cell junction integrity such that the KV lumen would fail to expand properly.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a prediction.

claim: Injection of either jupa MO efficiently reduced Jupa protein levels at KV cell junctions, as compared to embryos injected with a negative control MO.
source: Injection of either jupa MO efficiently reduced Jupa protein levels at KV cell junctions, as compared to embryos injected with a negative control MO (Figure 5A; Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Interfering with Jupa expression with MOs did not alter the gross morphology of embryos at 8 ss, but did disrupt KV lumen expansion relative to controls.
source: Interfering with Jupa expression with MOs did not alter the gross morphology of embryos at 8 ss, but did disrupt KV lumen expansion relative to controls (Figure 5C,D) as predicted.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5C,D.

claim: Delivering jupa MO specifically to the DFCs that give rise to KV also disrupted lumen expansion.
source: Delivering jupa MO specifically to the DFCs (Amack and Yost, 2004) that give rise to KV also disrupted lumen expansion (Figure 5C,D), indicating Jup functions cell-autonomously during KV morphogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5C,D and a supporting citation.

claim: Jup functions cell-autonomously during KV morphogenesis.
source: Delivering jupa MO specifically to the DFCs (Amack and Yost, 2004) that give rise to KV also disrupted lumen expansion (Figure 5C,D), indicating Jup functions cell-autonomously during KV morphogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data.

claim: The effect on KV lumen expansion caused by MO injection was significantly rescued by co-injection of full-length jupa mRNA.
source: Importantly, the effect on KV lumen expansion caused by MO injection was significantly rescued by co-injection of full-length jupa mRNA (Figure 5C,D; Figure 5—figure supplement 2B), indicating specificity for this phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5C,D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Expression of the JUP-naxos mRNA reduced KV lumen expansion without inducing other overt defects.
source: Similar to jupa MO treatments, expression of the JUP-naxos mRNA reduced KV lumen expansion without inducing other overt defects (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5C,D.

claim: The number of ciliated cells in KV in jupa MO and JUP-naxos mRNA treated embryos was similar to controls.
source: Importantly, the number of ciliated cells in KV in jupa MO and JUP-naxos mRNA treated embryos was similar to controls (Figure 5E; Figure 5—figure supplement 2C), which demonstrates that small KV lumen area was due to reduced lumen expansion rather than a reduced number of KV cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Small KV lumen area in jupa MO and JUP-naxos mRNA treated embryos was due to reduced lumen expansion rather than a reduced number of KV cells.
source: Importantly, the number of ciliated cells in KV in jupa MO and JUP-naxos mRNA treated embryos was similar to controls (Figure 5E; Figure 5—figure supplement 2C), which demonstrates that small KV lumen area was due to reduced lumen expansion rather than a reduced number of KV cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data.

claim: Reducing Jupa expression moderately reduced E-cadherin enrichment (~22% decrease) along KV cell lateral domains relative to controls.
source: First, we found that reducing Jupa expression moderately reduced E-cadherin enrichment (~22% decrease) along KV cell lateral domains relative to controls (Figure 5—figure supplement 3), which is consistent with previous results in cell culture studies (Fang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 3 and a supporting citation.

claim: Treatment of control MO embryos with CFTRact-09 significantly increased KV lumen area (~50%) as compared to DMSO.
source: Treatment of control MO embryos with CFTRact-09 significantly increased KV lumen area (~50%) as compared to DMSO, but a similar increase was not observed in Jupa depleted embryos (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5F.

claim: A similar increase in KV lumen area was not observed in Jupa depleted embryos treated with CFTRact-09.
source: Treatment of control MO embryos with CFTRact-09 significantly increased KV lumen area (~50%) as compared to DMSO, but a similar increase was not observed in Jupa depleted embryos (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5F.

claim: Fluids entering the lumen were leaking out through compromised cell-cell junctions in Jupa depleted embryos.
source: This suggested that fluids entering the lumen were leaking out through compromised cell-cell junctions.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results section based on the experimental data.

claim: In 4 out of 5 control MO embryos the dextran remained in the lumen over a 1 hr time period.
source: In 4 out of 5 control MO embryos the dextran remained in the lumen over a 1 hr time period.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 5G.

claim: In most Jupa depleted embryos the dextran gradually leaked out and only 1 out of 5 embryo retained significant amounts of dye.
source: Conversely, in most Jupa depleted embryos the dextran gradually leaked out and only 1 out of 5 embryo retained significant amounts of dye (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 5G.

claim: Jupa functions to maintain KV cell-cell adhesion integrity that is critical for KV lumen expansion.
source: Together, these results indicate Jupa functions to maintain KV cell-cell adhesion integrity that is critical for KV lumen expansion, and suggest Jupa depletion could provide a useful approach to block lumen expansion without affecting ion flux mediated cell volume changes in KV.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data.

claim: Jupa depletion could provide a useful approach to block lumen expansion without affecting ion flux mediated cell volume changes in KV.
source: Together, these results indicate Jupa functions to maintain KV cell-cell adhesion integrity that is critical for KV lumen expansion, and suggest Jupa depletion could provide a useful approach to block lumen expansion without affecting ion flux mediated cell volume changes in KV.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data.

claim: Asymmetric KV cell volume changes occurred between 2 ss and 8 ss in Jupa depleted embryos that were similar to controls.
source: Morphometric analyses of individual KV cells in mosaic-labeled Tg(sox17:CreERT2); Tg(ubi:Zebrabow) embryos treated with jupa MO-1 revealed that asymmetric KV cell volume changes occurred between 2 ss and 8 ss in Jupa depleted embryos (KV-ant cells increased volume from 2015 ± 534 μm3 to 2283 ± 414 μm3 and KV-post cells decreased volume from 1839 ± 612 μm3 to 1491 ± 310 μm3 that were similar to controls (KV-ant cells increased volume from 2108 ± 719 μm3 to 2709 ± 774 μm3 and KV-post cells decreased volume from 2273 ± 864 μm3 to 1434 ± 692 μm3) (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 6A,B.

claim: Even though the lumen failed to expand in Jupa depleted embryos, KV-ant and KV-post cells underwent normal asymmetric cell shape changes just as observed in control embryos between 2 ss to 8 ss.
source: 3D analysis of cell shapes—assessed using LWRs—indicated that even though the lumen failed to expand (Figure 6D; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), KV-ant and KV-post cells underwent normal asymmetric cell shape changes in Jupa depleted embryos just as observed in control embryos between 2 ss to 8 ss (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 6A,B,D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Cell shape changes can occur normally during KV remodeling in the absence of KV lumen expansion.
source: These results, which are consistent with predictions of the vertex models, provide in vivo evidence that cell shape changes can occur normally during KV remodeling in the absence of KV lumen expansion.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data.

claim: Analyses of mosaic-labeled KV cells in Lgl2 depleted embryos yielded results that were very similar to Jupa depleted embryos.
source: Analyses of mosaic-labeled KV cells in Lgl2 depleted embryos yielded results that were very similar to Jupa depleted embryos.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data in Figure 6C.

claim: Lgl2 depletion inhibited KV lumen expansion in mosaic labeled embryos.
source: Lgl2 depletion inhibited KV lumen expansion in mosaic labeled embryos (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), but KV cells completed normal asymmetric volume changes between 2 ss to 8 ss (KV-ant cells increased volume from 2057 ± 303 μm3 to 2329 ± 847 μm3 and KV-post cells decreased volume from 2127 ± 287 μm3 to 1617 ± 336 μm3) and normal asymmetric cell shape changes during KV remodeling (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 6C,D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In Lgl2 depleted embryos, KV cells completed normal asymmetric volume changes between 2 ss to 8 ss.
source: Lgl2 depletion inhibited KV lumen expansion in mosaic labeled embryos (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), but KV cells completed normal asymmetric volume changes between 2 ss to 8 ss (KV-ant cells increased volume from 2057 ± 303 μm3 to 2329 ± 847 μm3 and KV-post cells decreased volume from 2127 ± 287 μm3 to 1617 ± 336 μm3) and normal asymmetric cell shape changes during KV remodeling (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 6C.

claim: In Lgl2 depleted embryos, KV cells completed normal asymmetric cell shape changes during KV remodeling.
source: Lgl2 depletion inhibited KV lumen expansion in mosaic labeled embryos (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), but KV cells completed normal asymmetric volume changes between 2 ss to 8 ss (KV-ant cells increased volume from 2057 ± 303 μm3 to 2329 ± 847 μm3 and KV-post cells decreased volume from 2127 ± 287 μm3 to 1617 ± 336 μm3) and normal asymmetric cell shape changes during KV remodeling (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with reference to Figure 6C.

claim: Asymmetric epithelial cell shape changes that sculpt the KV organ are separable from the process of lumen expansion.
source: Taken together (for statistical power analysis, see Figure 6—source data 1), these results are consistent with Jupa knockdown results and indicate that asymmetric epithelial cell shape changes that sculpt the KV organ are separable from the process of lumen expansion.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data.

claim: Interfering with ion flux prevents KV lumen expansion, asymmetric changes in KV cell volume, and asymmetric changes in KV cell shape during KV remodeling.
source: Results from experimental perturbations (summarized in Figure 7) indicated that interfering with ion flux prevents KV lumen expansion, asymmetric changes in KV cell volume, and asymmetric changes in KV cell shape during KV remodeling.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with reference to Figure 7.

claim: When lumen expansion is inhibited with leaky KV cell-cell junctions, AP asymmetric KV cell shape changes occur normally.
source: Experimentally, we found that when we leave ion flux and asymmetric KV cell volume changes intact and only inhibit lumen expansion with leaky KV cell-cell junctions (summarized in Figure 7), AP asymmetric KV cell shape changes occur normally.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with reference to Figure 7.

claim: Asymmetric cell volume regulation is an intrinsic mechanism that guides cell shape changes during epithelial morphogenesis in KV.
source: Together, these studies identify asymmetric cell volume regulation as an intrinsic mechanism that guides cell shape changes during epithelial morphogenesis in KV.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the experimental and modeling results.

claim: Asymmetric cell volume regulation is a genetically programmed process that depends on the properties of surrounding cells, but can be separated from the biophysical forces of lumenogenesis.
source: We propose this is a genetically programmed process that depends on the properties of surrounding cells, but can be separated from the biophysical forces of lumenogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the experimental and modeling results.

claim: The finding that KV cells change volume during development is insightful for thinking about mechanisms of epithelial morphogenesis in KV since previous analyses that were limited to 2D did not predict differences in KV cell size.
source: The finding that KV cells change volume during development is insightful for thinking about mechanisms of epithelial morphogenesis in KV since previous analyses (Compagnon et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2012) that were limited to 2D did not predict differences in KV cell size.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: The AP asymmetry of volume changes is important for KV morphogenesis and function.
source: These results indicate the AP asymmetry of volume changes is important for KV morphogenesis and function.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the experimental results.

claim: Movement of fluids from epithelial cells into the lumen contributes to lumen expansion.
source: Decrease in cell volume has also been observed during morphogenesis of zebrafish otic vesicle (Hoijman et al., 2015), where it was suggested that movement of fluids from epithelial cells into the lumen contributes to lumen expansion.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Ion flux in KV establishes both transepithelial flows and intraepithelial flows from KV-post cells to fill the lumen.
source: Since the amount of volume lost by KV-post cells does not fully account for the increase in lumen size, we propose ion flux in KV establishes both transepithelial flows and intraepithelial flows from KV-post cells to fill the lumen.
evidence: This is a proposal stated in the discussion based on the experimental results.

claim: TOR signaling has been implicated in the morphogenesis of KV.
source: Interestingly, TOR signaling has been implicated in the morphogenesis of KV (Casar Tena et al., 2015; DiBella et al., 2009; Yuan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: Contractile force induced cell shape changes are instituted via cell volume reduction.
source: Interestingly, a recent study in Drosophila showed that contractile force induced cell shape changes are instituted via cell volume reduction (Saias et al., 2015), which indicates a link between cell volume regulation and mechanical force generation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Stretching the plasma membrane increased ion conductance and also the probability of open Cftr channels at cell membranes.
source: A recent study has uncovered mechanosensitive activation of Cftr in response to membrane stretch (Zhang et al., 2010). Stretching the plasma membrane increased ion conductance and also the probability of open Cftr channels at cell membranes.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: DFCs maintain their relative spatial positions throughout KV development.
source: By tracking the DFCs that give rise to KV, we have found that these cells maintain their relative spatial positions throughout KV development (Dasgupta and Amack, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Asymmetric volume changes are not alone sufficient to fully induce KV cell shape changes.
source: Our vertex model simulations suggest that asymmetric volume changes are not alone sufficient to fully induce KV cell shape changes.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the modeling results.

claim: Localized deposition of the ECM molecules laminin and fibronectin around anterior region of KV has been found to be important for asymmetric cell shape changes during KV morphogenesis.
source: Localized deposition of the ECM molecules laminin and fibronectin around anterior region of KV has been found to be important for asymmetric cell shape changes during KV morphogenesis (Compagnon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Asymmetric cell shape changes are more pronounced when anterior external cells had solid-like properties and posterior external cells were fluid-like.
source: Interestingly, our simulations indicated that asymmetric cell shape changes are more pronounced when anterior external cells had solid-like properties and posterior external cells were fluid-like.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the modeling results.

claim: Blocking lumen expansion with ion channel inhibitors prevents KV shape changes.
source: This idea is supported by the observation that blocking lumen expansion with ion channel inhibitors prevents KV shape changes (Compagnon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Lateral extension of KV-post cells can be uncoupled from the dorsoventral extensions, which play a critical role in lumen expansion.
source: Interestingly, lateral extension of KV-post cells can be uncoupled from the dorsoventral extensions, which play a critical role in lumen expansion.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the experimental results.

claim: Ion channels mediate asymmetric cell shape changes via lateral extension of KV-post cells even when overall lumen expansion is inhibited.
source: Inhibiting lumen expansion by altering junctional integrity hinders dorsoventral expansion of apical surfaces of all KV cells, but KV-post cells still lose their volume via ion channel mediated fluid efflux and undergo lateral extension to facilitate asymmetric KV cell shape changes (Figure 6). Thus, ion channels mediate asymmetric cell shape changes via lateral extension of KV-post cells even when overall lumen expansion is inhibited.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion with reference to Figure 6.

claim: Asymmetric KV cell shape changes depend on intrinsic ion flux-mediated fluid movements and do not depend on extrinsic forces generated by lumen expansion.
source: These results provide new mechanistic insight into KV epithelial morphogenesis and suggest a working model in which asymmetric KV cell shape changes depend on intrinsic ion flux-mediated fluid movements and do not depend on extrinsic forces generated by lumen expansion.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the experimental and modeling results.

claim: Luminal forces have a nominal impact on KV cell shape changes.
source: We propose that luminal forces have a nominal impact on KV cell shape changes.
evidence: This is a proposal stated in the discussion based on the experimental results.

claim: Inhibiting Rock2b function or non-muscle myosin II activity had no effect on KV lumen expansion, but prevented cell shape changes during KV remodeling.
source: First, KV cells can fail to change shape even when lumen expansion is normal. Inhibiting Rock2b function or non-muscle myosin II activity had no effect on KV lumen expansion, but prevented cell shape changes during KV remodeling (Wang et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: The mechanical forces generated during lumenogenesis are not sufficient to drive KV cell shape changes without active cytoskeletal contractility.
source: This indicates that the mechanical forces generated during lumenogenesis are not sufficient to drive KV cell shape changes without active cytoskeletal contractility.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on cited experimental results.

claim: The degree of KV lumen expansion is highly variable in a population of wild-type embryos.
source: Second, the degree of KV lumen expansion is highly variable in a population of wild-type embryos.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: The lumen only needs to exceed a relatively low size threshold for the KV to be functional.
source: Correlations between KV lumen size and KV function show that the lumen only needs to exceed a relatively low size threshold for the KV to be functional (Gokey et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Forces exerted by expansion of the lumen play a minor role in cell shape changes during KV epithelial morphogenesis.
source: Together, these findings suggest forces exerted by expansion of the lumen play a minor role in cell shape changes during KV epithelial morphogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the experimental results.

claim: KV cells are post-mitotic epithelial cells that assemble a cilium.
source: Thus it is important to note that KV cells are post-mitotic epithelial cells that assemble a cilium (Amack et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: During zebrafish otic vesicle development epithelial cells become thinner, suggesting intraepithelial fluid movement contributes to both lumen growth and cell/tissue shape change.
source: As mentioned previously, during zebrafish otic vesicle development epithelial cells become thinner, suggesting intraepithelial fluid movement contributes to both lumen growth and cell/tissue shape change (Hoijman et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Epithelial cells undergo cellular fluid loss to regulate cell volume and cell shape.
source: This finding is consistent with studies in cell culture systems (Braunstein et al., 2004; Vázquez et al., 2001) that have shown that epithelial cells indeed undergo cellular fluid loss to regulate cell volume and cell shape.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: A group of nonproliferative epithelial cells in the tooth primordium decrease their volume and become thinner during tooth budding morphogenesis.
source: In the mouse embryo, a group of nonproliferative epithelial cells in the tooth primordium also decrease their volume and become thinner during tooth budding morphogenesis (Ahtiainen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: During dorsal closure in Drosophila, cells within the amnioserosa lose their volume by ~30% and change their shape.
source: Another recent study in Drosophila uncovered that during dorsal closure cells within the amnioserosa lose their volume by ~30% and change their shape (Saias et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: In the egg chamber of Drosophila the follicle cell epithelium undergoes volume changes during oocyte development to attain distinct cell shapes.
source: Additionally, in the egg chamber of Drosophila the follicle cell epithelium undergoes volume changes during oocyte development to attain distinct cell shapes (Kolahi et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Cell volume change might be a common mechanism that impacts cell shape during epithelial morphogenesis in several tissues and organs.
source: Taken together with our experimental results and mathematical models in KV, these examples suggest that cell volume change might be a common mechanism that impacts cell shape during epithelial morphogenesis in several tissues and organs.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion based on the experimental results and literature.
